rows.label: Submit the American Studies major application
Twelve American Studies roster courses, 42+ credits
rows.note: The page gives no roster list, so this counts AMST courses and courses cross-listed with AMST, each worth at least 3 credits (the page says 3 or 4 credits each). The real roster may be wider, so this can read short but never generous. The cap of six courses per discipline is a separate confirm row, because the board cannot see each roster course's home discipline. Courses approved by the DUS from outside the roster do not show here; see the approvals row.

rows.label: Confirm with your advisor that no more than six of your twelve roster courses come from any one discipline
rows.note: Each roster course has a home discipline that the board cannot see, so this limit is yours to confirm.

rows.label: Every major course finished with a letter grade of C or higher
Six courses in a self-defined concentration area spanning at least two disciplines; confirm with your advisor
rows.note: The area is chosen with a faculty advisor, so the board cannot check it. These courses may also count toward other major requirements.

rows.label: Three courses focused substantially on pre-1900 material (9 to 12 credits); confirm which of your courses qualify
rows.note: No course list is given, so this is a confirm row. A course may count for this and the other distribution items.

rows.label: Two courses on American diversity (6 to 8 credits): social justice or inequality with attention to race, class, gender or sexuality; confirm which qualify
rows.note: No course list is given, so this is a confirm row. A course may overlap the pre-1900 item.

rows.label: One 4000-level American Studies seminar (not AMST 4998, 4993 or 4994)
rows.note: Also counts among the twelve roster courses (the page lets one course meet several distribution items). Any AMST 4000-4999 course counts except 4998, the honors tutorials 4993/4994, and three lecture-only courses seen in the offline catalog (death penalty, technology at work, poverty ethnography). The page lists no seminars, so a confirm row follows.

rows.label: Confirm with your advisor that your 4000-level American Studies course is a seminar
rows.note: The page requires a 4000-level seminar but does not list which 4000-level courses are seminars. Lecture-only courses seen in the offline catalog are left out above; a course from another term could still be a lecture, so check with your advisor that yours is a seminar.

rows.label: Up to two courses not cross-listed with American Studies may count only with Director of Undergraduate Studies approval
rows.note: The roster row above counts only AMST or cross-listed courses, so approved outside courses will not show there.

rows.label: Study abroad can give up to two courses (one semester) or three (a full year) toward the major with DUS approval; confirm yours
rows.note: Approved abroad courses are not AMST courses on the board, so they will not show in the roster row; the Director of Undergraduate Studies decides.
